critique: The black background and white particle color remain appropriate, but both frames still render as an extremely sparse starfield rather than the preset's dense, softly suspended floating-dust field. Frame t1 has only a few isolated points, and t4 has only roughly twenty visible particles, indicating that the active emission control is still effectively near 20 particles/sec despite the separate 9000 value. The occasional comparatively large bright dot also reads as a star rather than diffuse fine dust. Motion/population increases from t1 to t4, but the field is far too empty at the start and remains too sparse overall.

suggestions.why: This appears to be the active particles-per-second control: raising it from 20 will create an immediately populated field at t1 and a dense dust distribution by t4 instead of relying on the inactive/conflicting 9000 setting.
Reducing maximum particle size will prevent isolated oversized bright particles from reading as stars once emission density is increased, keeping the look predominantly fine floating dust.
